stem: A 12-day-old girl with a 46,XX karyotype has ambiguous genitalia. She is vomiting, dehydrated and feeding poorly. Sodium is low, potassium is high, and 17-hydroxyprogesterone is markedly raised. Her parents are healthy, and an older brother died at 2 weeks of age after vomiting and dehydration.
oneliner: 12-day-old 46,XX girl + ambiguous genitalia + vomiting, low Na, high K + high 17-hydroxyprogesterone + healthy parents, brother died in infancy → which gene?
ask: Which gene is most likely mutated?

whyNot.A: Excess 11-deoxycorticosterone retains salt, giving **hypertension**, not her **low sodium and high potassium**
whyNot.B: Loss blocks sex steroids, so a 46,XX girl would **not have ambiguous genitalia**, and 17-hydroxyprogesterone would be low
whyNot.D: Raises delta-5 precursors (17-hydroxypregnenolone), not **markedly raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone**; 46,XX girls are at most mildly virilized
whyNot.E: Makes **DHT**; defect undervirilizes **46,XY** infants and causes no salt wasting

why: Failure to make cortisol and aldosterone sends precursors toward androgens, which virilize a 46,XX fetus. **Raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone** with **salt wasting** marks **21-hydroxylase deficiency**, an **autosomal recessive** disorder of CYP21A2 (about 95% of CAH).

idea.rule: Raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone with salt wasting points to CYP21A2, inherited recessively.
also: Simple virilizing form: same gene, virilization without salt wasting
Non-classic form: same gene, hirsutism and irregular menses in young women
Both parents of an affected child are carriers (1 in 4 recurrence)
